narrative.text: It is your 45th birthday. Jonas and the children have prepared a small, private dinner in the residence. Vyktor, however, intercepts you in the hallway with a grim expression.

Chancellor, the economic crisis is the lead story on every channel. Pictures of you eating cake while the Kravenstal mills announce layoffs would be a disaster. I strongly advise canceling the dinner and working late in the office. Optics are everything.
It's your birthday, Katya. The children made cards. I made your favorite. Please don't let Vyktor's spreadsheets dictate every hour of our lives.

A birthday. A trivial thing in the grand machinery of state. But Jonas is right—I am drowning in spreadsheets and forgetting I have a family. Vyktor is also right—a photograph of a celebration during an economic downturn is ammunition for Kolvar. Do I embrace my family or protect my image?

choices.text: Have the private party with the family. Ignore Vyktor.
Cancel the party. Work late in the office.
Use ₭ 2,000 personal wealth to throw a massive public birthday festival to boost national morale.
